mainEntity.name: Should I spot-repair damaged knockdown texture or resurface the entire wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: A spot repair is ideal for isolated damage smaller than a few square feet, while full wall resurfacing makes sense if there are dozens of widespread patches or significant water damage. With a spot repair, you save time and money, but slight variations in texture or paint sheen might show under raking light. Resurfacing or skimming an entire wall creates a uniform look across the room, but requires moving all furniture, extensive masking, and longer dry times.
acceptedAnswer.description: Spot repairs work well for small, localized holes or cracks. If damage is widespread or under harsh angled light, re-texturing the entire surface ensures a seamless appearance.
